prompt: dustveil: A broad-winged moth of the Rot, grown as much as hatched: its pale wings are a living felt of fungal threads, dusted with spores, and they hang from it like a veil. It flies in short, fluttering hops, over walls and water alike, and drops to the ground to feed. Its grubs are timid things that nibble at sparse growth. The adults are not timid about anything: they eat cloth, wool first and then any natural fibre, worn or stored, and settle for grass only when nothing better is within reach. A tamed one can be shorn of a fine moth-silk, the fungal felt of its wings, provided the silk is kept well away from every other dustveil, which will eat that too. It is NOT an Earth animal: wings made of a felt of fungal threads instead of scaled membrane; wings dusted with spores; wings hang from the body like a veil. The north view stands with its feet on the same row as the east view's feet (measured: feet row -0.049 of canvas height from east's). The south view stands with its feet on the same row as the east view's feet (measured: feet row +0.055 of canvas height from east's). Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background.

A single RimWorld creature sprite, a harrok, on a transparent background, in painterly vanilla RimWorld style with broad brushstrokes and flat shaded color planes, realistic, with a clean moderately thick dark outline around the whole silhouette including every leg. The harrok is an invented desert ambush predator. Its narrow, slab-sided torso is held a man's height above the sand on four thin, very long legs, so the legs are far longer than the body is deep. Each leg ends in a splayed, spike-like foot with three long toes gripping the sand. The hide is bare, leathery and slightly plated, in dull sand-grey and ochre with darker banding along the back, with no fur, no tuft and no hooves. A long, flexible neck bends down from the front of the torso and carries an earless, elongated skull with a narrow beak-like jaw and small sunken dark eyes set low on the sides of the head; the jaw hangs low and still just above the sand, built to pluck small animals from the shadowed ground beneath the body. The short tail is a thin bare tapering rod. The creature stands motionless in an ambush pose and casts a long, thin shadow across the ground. Front view: eyes toward the viewer, the head lowered between the front legs. Side view: profile of the narrow torso, long neck and lowered head. Rear view, seen from behind: the haunches, the tail and the back of the neck, with the eyes hidden. Nothing in the animal resembles an Earth mammal: the silhouette is a tall narrow body on four stilt legs with a down-reaching neck and head.
